title: Internal Lateral Fast-Track & Skill-Bridging Protocol
author: Marina Lopez
body:
Overview:

This document defines the Fast-Track Lateral Transfer and Skill‑Bridging Protocol (the Protocol): a standardized, expedited process for moving existing Redwood employees between teams when business need and candidate readiness align. The Protocol balances speed with risk controls: it reduces time-to-mobility for high-impact moves while preserving quality through a lightweight assessment, manager commitments, and timeboxed ramp milestones.

Audience:
- Hiring managers and receiving team leads
- People Ops partners and recruiting coordinators
- Sending managers and career sponsors
- HRBP and compensation partners (when grade or comp changes are required)

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to internal candidates moving laterally (same band or ±1 band) or into adjacent functional areas where cross-skilling is feasible in 30–90 days.
- Excludes promotions that require formal promotion cycles (see promotions policy) and moves that change employment type (IC -> manager requires separate calibration).
- Not intended for external hires or contract conversions (see separate playbooks).

Principles:
- Candidate-first: preserve psychological safety and clear expectations for the participant.
- Timeboxed: target end-to-end cycle of 10 business days for intake-to-offer acceptance when all stakeholders are responsive.
- Outcome-based ramp: define concrete success criteria for 30/60/90 day checkpoints owned by the receiving manager.
- Minimal friction: reuse existing performance data, skip duplicative interviews where appropriate, and use a standard skill-bridging assessment.

Key roles and responsibilities:
- Sending manager: provide current performance summary, risks, and release date window.
- Receiving manager: define role scope, 30/60/90 success criteria, ramp plan, and assessment owner.
- People Ops (POPS): triage intake, ensure policy compliance, coordinate compensation/grade signoff, and document acceptance.
- Recruiting coordinator: schedule interviews and assessments when needed.
- Candidate: complete skill-bridge assessment and agree to ramp milestones and learning plan.

Fast-Track Intake checklist (intake completed by receiving manager + POPS):
1. Role metadata: title, band, hiring type (internal lateral), anticipated start date.
2. Business justification: 1–2 sentences describing why the transfer is needed now.
3. Core success criteria: 3 measurable outcomes for first 90 days.
4. Stakeholders and approvers: sending manager, receiving manager, POPS partner, comp approver (if band change).
5. Assessment gate: specify whether a light technical/skills assessment is required (guided rubric provided below).
6. Ramp support: training budget, shadowing pair, access requests, and mentor assignment.

Skill-bridging assessment (standardized, 60–120 minutes max):
- Purpose: quickly validate readiness and learning gaps. Not a replacement for formal interviews — its goal is to calibrate ramp plan.
- Format options (choose one):
  - Practical task (short take-home, 45–90 minutes) with rubric on execution and approach.
  - Paired working session (30–60 minutes) with receiving manager or senior IC.
  - Scenario-based interview (30 minutes) focused on cross-domain problem solving.
- Assessment rubric (apply 3-level rating: Ready / Needs Short Bridge / Needs Extended Bridge):
  - Ready: demonstrates independent ability to deliver 60–80% of 30-day success outcomes with minimal coaching.
  - Needs Short Bridge: will achieve outcomes with 2–4 weeks of directed training and mentorship.
  - Needs Extended Bridge: requires a >4 week plan or not appropriate for fast-track; escalate to standard hiring.

Decision matrix and timeline:
- Target turnaround: 10 business days from intake start to documented decision (offer / decline / redirect).
- If assessment = Ready -> receiving manager provides written offer within 2 business days and coordinates release window with sending manager.
- If Needs Short Bridge -> offering manager documents the 30-day bridge plan and issues offer with attached bridge plan.
- If Needs Extended Bridge -> decline fast-track and recommend formal job posting or extended rotation; POPS documents rationale.

Offer and release steps (numbered):
1. Receiving manager drafts internal offer email using template (see below) and includes 30/60/90 success criteria and bridge plan if applicable.
2. Sending manager and receiving manager agree on release date (typical windows: immediate, 2 weeks, end of sprint).
3. POPS updates HR systems (internal transfer), submits any comp signoffs, and schedules a joint handoff meeting.
4. Candidate accepts offer in writing (email) and is copied into handoff and access request tickets.

Manager commitments and ramp plan template (to be populated at offer):
- First 30 days: onboarding checklist, explicit owner for daily check-ins (first 2 weeks), mandatory shadowing hours (min 8 hours), and a defined starter project with acceptance criteria.
- First 60 days: ownership of a deliverable and a demo for stakeholders; monthly skip-level touchpoint scheduled.
- First 90 days: endorsement decision criteria for team fit and sustained independent contribution; calibrate comp or band changes if needed.

30/60/90 checkpoint rubric (manager uses this to document progress):
- Metrics to capture: progress vs success criteria (percent complete), blockers, learning activities completed, mentor feedback, and recommended next steps.
- Outcome flags: On-Track / At-Risk / Not-Meeting-Expectation. If At-Risk at 30 days, an intensified remediation plan is required; POPS must be looped in and a new 30-day remediation milestone set.

Access and onboarding operational items (runbook snippet):
- Access requests: request standard role-based permissions the week before start date (Jira, Slack channels, code repos).
- Hardware: if cross-team equipment change needed, raise a hardware ticket 5 business days before start date.
- Learning resources: link new-hire handbooks and the receiving team’s knowledge base page.

Compensation & banding guidance:
- If the move does not change band or comp: no approvals beyond POPS confirmation required.
- If band or comp change is requested: receiving manager must attach comp case and route to Compensation within 3 business days; fast-track may be paused until signoff but ramp plan can proceed at existing comp pending approval.

Manager email offer template (internal):
Subject: Internal Transfer Offer – [Candidate Name] to [Team Name]\n
Hi [Candidate Name],\n\nWe’re excited to invite you to join [Team Name] as [New Title] with an anticipated start date of [Start Date]. Attached are the 30/60/90 success criteria and your onboarding plan. Your receiving manager will be [Manager Name] and your mentor will be [Mentor Name]. Please confirm acceptance by replying to this thread by [Date, 2 business days].\n\nWelcome (again),\n[Manager Name]\n
Escalation and exceptions:
- If sending manager has release concerns, escalate to people-ops escalation lead within 24 hours.
- If assessment or decision timeline exceeds 10 business days due to business-critical constraints, the receiving manager must document extended timeline and approval from the POPS partner.

Monitoring success (metrics POPS will track quarterly):
- Time-to-transfer (median days intake→start) target: <= 14 business days for accepted fast-track moves.
- 30-day On-Track rate target: >= 85% for fast-track participants.
- Retention at 6 months target: >= 92% for lateral transfers.
- Manager satisfaction (survey): median >= 4.2/5 across moves.

Example scenarios (illustrative):
- Scenario A — SW Eng IC moving to infra tools team: assessment = paired session (45 min); rating = Needs Short Bridge; bridge plan = 3 weeks of pairing + code walkthroughs; offer issued with bridge plan attached.
- Scenario B — PM moving to Growth PM role: assessment = scenario interview; rating = Ready; offer issued and start date set in 10 business days.

Appendices:
A. Short intake form (fields to paste into ticket): Role title; Band; Business justification (1–2 lines); Candidate name; Sending manager; Anticipated start; Assessment type; Success criteria (3 bullets); Ramp support items.

B. Assessment rubric (table):
- Dimension: Technical aptitude / Domain knowledge / Learning agility / Communication
- Rating labels: Ready | Needs Short Bridge | Needs Extended Bridge

C. Sample 30‑day check-in template (to copy into performance notes):
- Date:
- Progress vs criteria (percent):
- Completed learning activities:
- Blockers and mitigation:
- Mentor feedback summary:
- Outcome flag: On-Track / At-Risk / Not-Meeting-Expectation:
- Actions (owner + due date):

- Promotions and banding guidance (see: /confluence/people-ops/promotion-pathways-and-calibration-protocol-2026)
- New hire onboarding checklist (see: /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-immersion-rotation-playbook-2026)

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Can a candidate decline the fast-track and opt for a formal posting?
A: Yes. Candidates retain choice; POPS will support the alternative path.

Q: What if the sending manager objects?
A: Objections should be raised within 48 hours. POPS mediates and may delay release if operational risk is material.

Q: Who pays for training during bridge period?
A: Receiving team covers short, role-specific micro-training; for larger training budgets, comp partner approval is required.

Document ownership and review cadence:
- Owner: People Ops – Internal Mobility (Marina Lopez).
- Review cadence: annual or sooner if metrics fall outside targets.

Contact:
- For questions or intake submissions, email people-ops-internal-mobility@redwood.ai or contact your POPS partner.
